analysis:
Examined LaunchAgent.swift base and head plus the test patch. The only production change adds two keys, ToolStreamPreparation.streamToolCallsEnvironmentKey and ReasoningPromptProbe.plainTailContentSeedEnvironmentKey, to inferencePassthroughEnvKeys (head lines 284-298). passthroughEnvKeys concatenates that list (head 300-313). passthroughEnvironment (head 327-348) forwards only non-empty values of allowlisted keys into the launchd plist EnvironmentVariables. The two keys are tuning rollbacks, whose doc comment (head 284-286) says exact 0 disables them. They are not credentials, endpoints, attestation or authorization inputs, and no secret passthrough is added. The App Attest worker opt-in handling (head 335-339) is unchanged and still persists only the exact value 1. The launchd control flow is unchanged: stop/disable, restart, bootout waiting, KeepAlive=false, RunAtLoad=true and ExitTimeOut. Relevant threat entries are TB-003, TB-011 and T-053. The change adds no new trust boundary. The plist and its environment are already writable by the local operator, who is the adversary in TB-003, so the added keys confer no new authority.

The test patch (EngineV2ProductionWiringTests.swift line 312) only extends a switch to cover the new .toolCallDelta event and has no security impact.

Unverified contract: I did not see ToolStreamPreparation or the new toolCallDelta streaming path. Incremental tool-call streaming could affect the E2E encrypted response path (T-008) or tool-call parsing and output handling, but that code is outside the supplied units. The next pass should check that tool-call deltas pass through the same encryption and fail-closed path as other chunks. It should also check that the default-on behavior has no plaintext-leak or unbounded-resource implications.
